subject: Learning Methods
title: Chronic Partial Sleep Restriction
description: Learn Chronic Partial Sleep Restriction in one minute.

hook.text: Sleeping six hours a night for two weeks produces the same cognitive deficit as two full nights of total sleep.

buildup.text: Chronic partial sleep restriction is widespread. Most adults sleep fewer than seven hours.

discovery.text: Unlike acute deprivation, chronic sleep debt doesn't feel dramatic. You adapt to the diminished state and call it.

twist.text: You can't fully repay sleep debt with weekend catch-up. While partial recovery occurs, the learning deficit from.

climax.text: Aim for seven to nine hours consistently. Not on average, not on weekends.

punchline.text: Six hours feels fine. It is not. The deficit hides.

quiz.question: Why is chronic partial sleep restriction especially harmful for students?
options: It causes permanent brain damage after two weeks
The cumulative deficit equals total sleep deprivation but feels normal
It only affects physical performance, not mental ability
